clue.text: They were believed to control Winston

definitions.text: They were believed to control Winston

parts.words: They were believed to control Winston
parts.note: Winston is Winston Smith, hero of Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, watched by the Party's mind-reading enforcers, not Churchill

explanation.surface: A remark about who really pulled the strings on Churchill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winston' suggests Churchill, but it is Winston Smith of Orwell's novel, whose private ideas were policed by the state.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's novel these officers hunt down forbidden ideas, so they are believed to control the hero's mind.

clue.text: A place on the course Auntie used to run

definitions.text: A place on the course Auntie used to run

parts.words: A place on the course Auntie used to run
parts.note: Auntie is the BBC's nickname; a place on a racecourse sounds like a finishing position, and a course is also a schedule of broadcasts the BBC once ran

explanation.surface: An aunt's old running track and where she finished on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC, which ran a cultural radio network under this name from 1946 to 1967; 'third' is a placing in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC's former cultural radio service was a broadcasting channel it ran, named with a race placing.

clue.text: Moving to the end of the course, the head is on target, just

indicators.note: these words tell us to shift a letter from its place to the back of the word for course
the head is the first letter of the word for course, the one that travels

parts.note: a route is a course taken

explanation.surface: Instructions to someone shooting arrows at the far end of a range.
explanation.walkthrough: In archery or shooting the outer is the ring just outside the bull, so a shot there is on target, but only just.
explanation.definitionFit: The outermost scoring ring of a target, so a hit there barely counts as a hit.

clue.text: A pair of old women, primly virtuous

indicators.note: a pair means the piece is written out twice in a row

parts.note: goody, short for goodwife, is an old title for a woman of humble rank

explanation.surface: Two elderly ladies of strict and proper habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goody' was the old courtesy title for a married woman of lowly station, as in Goody Proctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A smugly well-behaved person is called this, so it describes priggish, self-righteous virtue.

clue.text: Tawdry covering for plain fabric

indicators.note: covering means the word for tawdry wraps around the word for plain

parts.note: tat is cheap, tawdry stuff
bare means plain, unadorned

explanation.surface: A cheap cover thrown over a plain bit of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Tabaret is a striped upholstery silk.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped silk used for upholstery is a kind of woven textile.

clue.text: Greek who gave no peace to opponents

parts.note: the letter O looks like zero, or nothing
rest is peace and quiet
in bridge East and South sit as opponents, E and S

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek warrior who harried his enemies relentlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Orestes was himself given no peace, pursued by the Furies after killing his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Orestes is a hero of Greek myth, son of Agamemnon.

clue.text: Turn over in bed perhaps

definitions.meaning: of an engine, to tick over without doing work
lazing around, as one might be when lying in

explanation.surface: Advice to shift position when lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine ticking over runs without load, and someone lounging in bed is doing nothing: both senses mean inactive.

clue.text: Went topless, offering drinks and giving embraces

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of Went is removed

parts.note: wining means supplying wine to guests

explanation.surface: A risque party where someone went topless while serving drinks and hugging guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Twining around someone is embracing them, so the word describes the action of hugging.

clue.text: Birds on wrong course got famously stranded

parts.note: robins are birds

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of course are put in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Migrating birds that flew off course and ended up stuck somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is a link. Defoe's castaway is the most famous shipwrecked man in fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's fictional castaway lived for years marooned on an island, the archetype of a shipwrecked man.

clue.text: Alas, expecting international currency

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: A lament that someone is anticipating a global money supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' looks like awaiting, but it means pregnant: an old euphemism for an unmarried girl who is pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphemism: an unmarried girl pregnant was said to be in difficulty, so a regretful 'expecting' carries the sense.

clue.text: Black out from being drunk — a chancy business

indicators.note: out means the letter for black is taken away from the word for drunk

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone passing out after drinking too much, a risky way to behave.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery-style game of numbers drawn at random is a game of pure luck.

clue.text: In time. Christian is accepted by prejudiced young lady

definitions.text: In time. Christian is accepted by prejudiced young lady

indicators.note: being accepted by means being taken inside, so the Christian goes inside the time

parts.note: a day is a period of time
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic, a Christian

explanation.surface: A prim young woman eventually warms to a Christian suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: In Pride and Prejudice, Elizabeth Bennet, the prejudiced young lady, misjudges Mr Darcy but eventually accepts his proposal; 'is accepted by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: In Austen's novel the proud hero is at last taken as husband by the heroine who misjudged him.

clue.text: From parrot, expected repetition

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words parrot expected

explanation.surface: A parrot can be counted on to repeat what it hears.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by mechanical repetition is learning by heart without understanding.

clue.text: Two girls share

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: A pair of girls splitting something between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divi' is British slang for a dividend, a share of profits.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a dividend, the portion of profits paid out to each holder.

clue.text: Calling back about work

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a vocation is one's work or calling

explanation.surface: Phoning someone back about a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' tempts as the clue for VOCATION, but it is part of the definition; 'work' gives VOCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Revoking something is withdrawing or recalling it.

clue.text: Criticise wine taken from bond

parts.note: to rap is to criticise sharply
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Complaining about wine taken out of a bonded warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bond' suggests a bonded warehouse where wine is stored, but it means a close relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A close harmonious understanding between people is a connection or tie.

clue.text: Exam can be such a joke

definitions.meaning: a hands-on test, as opposed to a written paper
a prank played physically on someone

explanation.surface: A test so easy it is laughable.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on test and a physical prank are both described by this adjective meaning concerned with doing.

clue.text: Sort of creature that's seen in glasses

indicators.note: being seen in means placed inside the word for glasses

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A creature that can be made out through spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological category of organisms that interbreed, a kind of animal.

clue.text: A very good morning, old lady

parts.note: grand means excellent, very good

explanation.surface: Cheerily greeting an elderly woman early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a grandmother, an elderly woman.

clue.text: Thus bound, perhaps, for part of Africa

definitions.meaning: books are often bound in fine goatskin leather of this name

explanation.surface: Someone heading off to a corner of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound for' looks like heading towards; it is a bookbinding in that leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African kingdom, and the goatskin leather named after it used for bookbinding.

clue.text: A sort of wedding when daughter is 9?

definitions.text: A sort of wedding when daughter is 9?

parts.words: A sort of wedding when daughter is 9?
parts.note: the cross-reference points to the expression for being pregnant out of wedlock, when a father might force a hasty marriage

explanation.surface: A hurried marriage arranged because the bride is pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across means pregnant; a wedding forced by the bride's father, figuratively at gunpoint, takes this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasty marriage forced by a pregnancy, as if the bride's father held a firearm.

clue.text: Heavenly colour, ordered in bulk? Yes

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Buying paint of a celestial shade in large quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like bought, but it is the anagram signal on BULK plus YES.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale blue like a clear daytime heaven.

clue.text: Culturally pretentious, but my follower is oddly moved

indicators.note: oddly moved means the letters are shuffled into a strange order

parts.note: the clue that follows this one, 22 across, whose answer supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A snob whose hanger-on behaves strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my follower' means the next entry, 22 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Showily affecting an interest in art and culture.

clue.text: Pronounced characteristic one used to carry

indicators.note: pronounced tells us to take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic; in British speech its final T is often silent

explanation.surface: A marked feature of someone who carries things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' reads as strongly marked, but it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat board with a rim on which food and drink are carried.

clue.text: Flower sported by a bad poet

definitions.text: Flower sported by a bad poet

parts.words: Flower sported by a bad poet
parts.note: a bad poet is a ..., a word that ends with the name of a daisy-like bloom, as if wearing it

explanation.surface: A mediocre versifier wearing a bloom in a buttonhole.
explanation.walkthrough: A poetaster is an inferior poet, and the flower is the last five letters of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like garden bloom, often purple, flowering in autumn.

clue.text: Speaking in place of designated people

indicators.note: speaking tells us we want the sound of the word

parts.note: there means in that place

explanation.surface: A spokesperson standing in for named individuals.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessive pronoun meaning belonging to the people mentioned.

clue.text: Turns leaves

definitions.meaning: ... as a noun, chances to play in a game

explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun for players' chances, and a verb meaning departs.

clue.text: Computer fails to print edges of foreign letter

indicators.note: failing to print the edges means the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: omicron is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A printer fault that cuts off the margins of a letter written in another language.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form for a small personal computing machine.

clue.text: Visitors accepting a little money will take your measure

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the visitors enclose the rest

parts.note: callers are visitors
a means one, the Roman numeral I
p is a penny, a small coin in British currency

explanation.surface: Guests who take a small tip and then size you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take your measure' sounds like judging someone; it is literal for this measuring instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-legged instrument for measuring diameters or thickness.

clue.text: Can't find your sauce? Get bottle out!'

parts.note: to mislay one's own possession
nerve means cheek, sauce, impudence

explanation.surface: Someone who has run out of a condiment and is told to fetch a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, and to 'bottle out' is to back off through fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To bottle out is British slang for losing courage at the last moment.
